newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bourse ends weekly trading 2.8 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bourse ends weekly trading 2.8 pct higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed the week on Friday 2.8 percent higher with more buyers than sellers, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 570.96 points from 555.22 points last Friday.
"There were more people interested, much funds under mangement but not enough shares for everybody," a broker at the Casablanca-based Sogebourse said.

ONA group, the country's largest non-state holding, closed at 720 dirhams from 701 dirhams, the week before. ONA is expected to show an estimated 800 million dirhams net profits for 1996, a market analyst said.
The group's results will be released by mid-April, the analyst said.
In the banking sector, Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed at 561 dirhams from 490 dirhams.
"During Friday session, some 12,000 shares were exchanged on the off market,"the Sogebourse broker said.
Sogebourse said this week German bank Commerzbank had increased its stake in BMCE to 10 percent from 1.6 percent.
Leading stock Wafabank traded at 750 dirhams from 725 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed at 203 dirhams from 190 dirhams last week.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing, which was listed on the bourse late in February took 41 dirhams on the week to close at 312.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 678 dirhams from 665 dirhams last Friday.
Newly-floated credit firm Credor rose to 650 dirhams from 645 dirhams last week.
Traded volume on the official market was from 69.6 million dirhams 49.6 million dirhams last Friday.
